title: Example 124: a partitioner rewritten with floorMod, refuted by the tool's own checker in the second stage of its search
description: Runs build.py on example 124, a B9 regression proof on Crosscut's kafka.Partitioner#partitionFor with approach.engine native: the masked remainder (hash & 0x7fffffff) % n rewritten as Math.floorMod(hash, n). The tool's own bounded model checker (lib/src/bmc, CaDiCaL) explores the harness path by path and, on the violating path, asks for an input in the stages JBMC is run through ([0:20], then [-100000:100000], then everything), reporting the stage. Non-negative hashes agree, so the witness comes from the second stage and the interpreter shrinks it. The library's run of this shape took 0.4 s and shrank the witness to partitionFor(hash=-1, numPartitions=3), 1 before and 2 after.
expected: verdict violation; a counterexample with a negative hash, before and after partitions differing; the proof line says found by jvmcontract's own checker ... searching inputs in [-100000:100000]
